Change c0186. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. VIII.

Context before (unchanged): Anguish and despair had penetrated into the core of my heart; I bore a hell within me, which nothing could extinguish.

1818 text: We staid several hours with Justine; and it was with great difficulty that Elizabeth could tear herself away.

1831 text: We stayed several hours with Justine; and it was with great difficulty that Elizabeth could tear herself away.

Diff: We [-staid-] {+stayed+} several hours with Justine; and it was with great difficulty that Elizabeth could tear herself away.

Context after (unchanged): "I wish," cried she, "that I were to die with you; I cannot live in this world of misery."

result.rationale: Change is only the archaic past-tense form 'staid' to modern 'stayed'; the verb, meaning, and events are identical, so this is orthographic modernization with no interpretive weight.
